I built the first playable maze game and pushed it to the open PR #11: https://github.com/fischerq/ludumdare60/pull/11.

**What's in it**
- **Our own Pac-Man-style game, full screen:** a 19×25 maze with a tunnel that wraps around the sides, blue glowing walls and a pixel font. Clearing the maze shows a placeholder "something is behind the glass" screen where the first layer will go.
- **Ghosts:** four of them, each with a simplified version of the original chase behaviour. They take turns chasing and retreating to their corners. Power pellets turn them blue (flashing near the end), and eaten ghosts float back to the house as eyes.
- **Controls:** swipe anywhere to turn. A turn waits until it fits, reversing is instant, and you can keep swiping without lifting your finger. Arrow keys or WASD work on a laptop.
- **Rest of the game:** 3 lives, score and high score.
- **Sound:** generated in the browser, no audio files. There's a start jingle, the waka on dots, a power-pellet sound and a wobble while ghosts are blue, plus sounds for eating a ghost, dying and clearing the maze.
- **Code shape:** the game rules have no Phaser in them (`src/systems/maze.js`), so lab benches and later layers can reuse them. All numbers and the maze layout are in `src/config.js`.

**Checks:** a headless run of 30 games with random steering had no crashes, every dot is reachable and the maze has no dead ends. In a phone-sized browser the game ran with no errors and a swipe steered correctly. **Layer docs**

*Inside the screen (zoom in)*, in `design/systems/layer-crt.md`, starts with notes on how arcade screens work. I wrote them from general knowledge without a web search, to save tokens, and marked them to be fact-checked before any of it appears in the game. The main points:
- **Rotated monitor:** the Pac-Man monitor is mounted on its side, so its lines run vertically across the playfield.
- **The beam:** it draws one line at a time, about 15,700 lines per second, and a full picture about 60 times a second.
- **Phosphor:** each dot glows only right after the beam hits it and fades within milliseconds. That is what "dots are only edible while lit" maps onto.
- **The game tick:** the game moves everything while the beam jumps back to the top, 60 times a second. That ties in nicely with a later code layer.
- **Failure modes to borrow as mechanics:** burn-in, a rolling picture when sync is lost, colour fringes, degaussing, and the high voltage inside the tube.

The doc also records your ideas: a Pac in a different skin, the game above playing itself and lighting up the pixels, dots edible only while lit, and the refresh beam as the hazard.
